# _autosummary/mergeset.log.html.md

# mergeset.log

The evaluation log: append-only JSONL, and the single source of truth.

Every expensive evaluation is written here once and never re-run. The log also
carries the *monotone closure*: because good sets are (approximately) downward
closed, a passing set marks all of its subsets known-good, and a failing set
marks all of its supersets known-bad. That closure is computed lazily from the
stored rows rather than materialized, so the file stays small and honest.

Monotonicity is a strong prior, not a law: a change may contain the fix that
makes another change work, and flaky tests break it outright. Violations are
detected and reported ([`EvaluationLog.monotonicity_violations()`](_autosummary/mergeset.log.html.md#mergeset.log.EvaluationLog.monotonicity_violations)) instead of
being silently trusted.

A row is an answer about *commits*, not about ids. Once the log is pinned
([`EvaluationLog.pin()`](_autosummary/mergeset.log.html.md#mergeset.log.EvaluationLog.pin)) to the base and the head of each change in play,
only rows evaluated against those same commits count — rows about an older head
of a rewritten branch are kept on disk and in [`EvaluationLog.rows`](_autosummary/mergeset.log.html.md#mergeset.log.EvaluationLog.rows), and
simply not matched (i2mint/mergeset#23). The same holds for *what* was run:
rows judged by another validator (another command, other stages) are kept and
not matched (i2mint/mergeset#32).

### Functions

| [`sets_evaluated`](_autosummary/mergeset.log.html.md#mergeset.log.sets_evaluated)(log)   | Yield `(sorted ids, verdict)` for every row — handy for reports.   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Classes

| [`EvaluationLog`](_autosummary/mergeset.log.html.md#mergeset.log.EvaluationLog)([store, pins, trust_unpinned])   | Append-only record of evaluations, plus the monotone closure over it.                                 |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`JsonlLines`](_autosummary/mergeset.log.html.md#mergeset.log.JsonlLines)(path)                               | Append-only sequence of JSON objects backed by one file.                                              |
| [`Known`](_autosummary/mergeset.log.html.md#mergeset.log.Known)(verdict[, exact, witness])               | What the log already knows about a set, without re-evaluating it.                                     |
| [`MemoryLines`](_autosummary/mergeset.log.html.md#mergeset.log.MemoryLines)([iterable])                        | In-memory stand-in for [`JsonlLines`](_autosummary/mergeset.log.html.md#mergeset.log.JsonlLines) (tests, dry runs). |
| [`Pins`](_autosummary/mergeset.log.html.md#mergeset.log.Pins)(base, heads[, validator, resolver])       | What a question is about: the base, each change's head sha, the validator.                            |
| [`StoreLines`](_autosummary/mergeset.log.html.md#mergeset.log.StoreLines)(store, key)                         | Lines backed by one key of a `MutableMapping` — the non-file backend.                                 |

### *class* mergeset.log.EvaluationLog(store=None, , pins=None, trust_unpinned=False)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Append-only record of evaluations, plus the monotone closure over it.

* **Parameters:**
  * **store** ([`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)) – Persistence seam. A path (str/PathLike) is wrapped in
    [`JsonlLines`](_autosummary/mergeset.log.html.md#mergeset.log.JsonlLines); pass [`StoreLines`](_autosummary/mergeset.log.html.md#mergeset.log.StoreLines) to put the log in an
    artifact store (S3 and friends), or [`MemoryLines`](_autosummary/mergeset.log.html.md#mergeset.log.MemoryLines) for an
    ephemeral log. With no argument at all the log goes to the artifact
    store’s `evaluations/adhoc.jsonl` — never the working directory.
  * **pins** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Pins`](_autosummary/mergeset.log.html.md#mergeset.log.Pins)]) – The commits the questions are about (see [`Pins`](_autosummary/mergeset.log.html.md#mergeset.log.Pins) and
    [`pin()`](_autosummary/mergeset.log.html.md#mergeset.log.EvaluationLog.pin)). Unpinned, every row counts, as before pinning existed;
    [`mergeset.analyze()`](_autosummary/mergeset.html.md#mergeset.analyze) always pins.
  * **trust_unpinned** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Let rows that record no commits at all (written before
    i2mint/mergeset#23, or by an unpinned log), or no validator while
    the pins name one (written before i2mint/mergeset#32), count as
    matches once the log is pinned. Off by default, because such a row
    may be about a head that has since moved, or judged by a command
    that has since changed — which is the defect pinning exists to
    close. Turn it on only when you know neither has changed since those
    rows were written; it is the migration path for an old log. A row
    whose recorded commits or validator differ never counts.

```pycon
>>> log = EvaluationLog(MemoryLines())
>>> from mergeset.base import Evaluation, Verdict
>>> _ = log.record(Evaluation(frozenset({'a', 'b'}), Verdict.PASS))
>>> bool(log.known(frozenset({'a'})))          # subset of a passing set
True
>>> log.known(frozenset({'a'})).verdict.value
'pass'
>>> _ = log.record(Evaluation(frozenset({'c', 'd'}), Verdict.FAIL))
>>> log.known(frozenset({'a', 'c', 'd'})).verdict.value   # superset of a failing set
'fail'
>>> log.known(frozenset({'a', 'c'})).verdict is None
True
```

#### caching(evaluate, , infer_pass=True)

Wrap `evaluate` so known sets are answered from the log.

The returned callable is what the solver should be handed: it never
spends a real evaluation on a set the log can already decide.

`infer_pass=False` runs a set whose PASS would only be *inferred*
from a passing superset, and records it: for a caller that needs an
exact PASS behind every claim (a cheaper tier on the way to a deeper
one). Exact rows and inferred FAILs are still answered from the log.

```pycon
>>> log = EvaluationLog(MemoryLines())
>>> _ = log.record(Evaluation(frozenset('ab'), Verdict.PASS))
>>> runs = []
>>> def run(s):
...     runs.append(set_key(s))
...     return Evaluation(s, Verdict.PASS)
>>> log.caching(run)(frozenset('a')).cached, runs
(True, [])
>>> log.caching(run, infer_pass=False)(frozenset('a')).cached, runs
(False, [('a',)])
```

#### exact(subset)

The most recent evaluation of exactly this set, if any.

* **Return type:**
  [`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Evaluation`](_autosummary/mergeset.base.html.md#mergeset.base.Evaluation)]

#### *property* failing *: [List](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.List)[[frozenset](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#frozenset)]*

Sets recorded as bad, smallest first (smallest are the most useful).

#### known(subset)

What we know about `subset` without evaluating it.

Exact hits win; otherwise the monotone closure decides, preferring the
cheapest witness (the largest passing superset, the smallest failing
subset).

* **Return type:**
  [`Known`](_autosummary/mergeset.log.html.md#mergeset.log.Known)

#### maximal_passing_sets()

Recorded passing sets with no recorded passing proper superset.

* **Return type:**
  [`List`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.List)[[`frozenset`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#frozenset)]

#### minimal_failing_sets()

Recorded failing sets with no recorded failing proper subset.

These are the *conflicts* the solver hits. They are minimal with respect
to what has been observed, which is not necessarily globally minimal —
the solver shrinks them further with QuickXplain as it goes.

* **Return type:**
  [`List`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.List)[[`frozenset`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#frozenset)]

#### monotonicity_violations()

`(good, bad)` pairs where a *subset* of a good set was seen failing.

A non-empty result means the downward-closure assumption broke here:
a flaky test, a non-deterministic build, or a change that *fixes*
another. Reported, never silently smoothed over.

* **Return type:**
  [`List`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.List)[[`Tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Tuple)[[`frozenset`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#frozenset), [`frozenset`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#frozenset)]]

#### *property* other_resolver *: [List](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.List)[[Evaluation](_autosummary/mergeset.base.html.md#mergeset.base.Evaluation)]*

The [`stale`](_autosummary/mergeset.log.html.md#mergeset.log.EvaluationLog.stale) rows whose outcome another resolver decided.

An assisted PASS read by a run without the resolver, or a conflict
recorded without one read by a run with one (i2mint/mergeset#34).

#### *property* other_validator *: [List](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.List)[[Evaluation](_autosummary/mergeset.base.html.md#mergeset.base.Evaluation)]*

The [`stale`](_autosummary/mergeset.log.html.md#mergeset.log.EvaluationLog.stale) rows judged by a validator other than the pinned one.

Usually a tier or `--validate-command` whose command was edited.

#### *property* passing *: [List](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.List)[[frozenset](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#frozenset)]*

Sets recorded as good, largest first.

#### pin(, base, heads, validator=None, resolver=None)

Scope *this* log to `base`, these heads and `validator`; returns `self`.

`validator` is the fingerprint of what the questions will be asked of
([`mergeset.validation.fingerprint_of()`](_autosummary/mergeset.validation.html.md#mergeset.validation.fingerprint_of)); `None` matches rows on
commits alone. `resolver` is how their sets are merged
([`mergeset.oracle.resolver_fingerprint_of()`](_autosummary/mergeset.oracle.html.md#mergeset.oracle.resolver_fingerprint_of)): rows whose outcome a
different resolver decided stop counting; `None` ignores it.

[`pinned()`](_autosummary/mergeset.log.html.md#mergeset.log.EvaluationLog.pinned) is the same without changing this object.

From here on, reading ([`known()`](_autosummary/mergeset.log.html.md#mergeset.log.EvaluationLog.known), [`exact()`](_autosummary/mergeset.log.html.md#mergeset.log.EvaluationLog.exact), the closure,
iteration, `len`) sees only rows evaluated against these commits, and
[`record()`](_autosummary/mergeset.log.html.md#mergeset.log.EvaluationLog.record) stamps new rows with them. Nothing is removed: the other
rows stay in the store and in [`rows`](_autosummary/mergeset.log.html.md#mergeset.log.EvaluationLog.rows), and are reported by
[`stale`](_autosummary/mergeset.log.html.md#mergeset.log.EvaluationLog.stale) and [`unpinned`](_autosummary/mergeset.log.html.md#mergeset.log.EvaluationLog.unpinned).

* **Return type:**
  [`EvaluationLog`](_autosummary/mergeset.log.html.md#mergeset.log.EvaluationLog)

```pycon
>>> from mergeset.base import Evaluation, Verdict
>>> log = EvaluationLog(MemoryLines()).pin(base='B', heads={'a': 'A1'})
>>> _ = log.record(Evaluation(frozenset('a'), Verdict.PASS))
>>> log.known(frozenset('a')).verdict.value
'pass'
>>> _ = log.pin(base='B', heads={'a': 'A2'})   # branch a was rewritten
>>> log.known(frozenset('a')).verdict is None, len(log.rows), len(log.stale)
(True, 1, 1)
```

#### pinned(, base, heads, validator=None, resolver=None, trust_unpinned=None)

A view of this log scoped to `base`, these heads and `validator`.

Same store, same rows; this log itself is left as it was, so a caller
that hands one log to two analyses keeps its own view of it.

* **Return type:**
  [`EvaluationLog`](_autosummary/mergeset.log.html.md#mergeset.log.EvaluationLog)

```pycon
>>> from mergeset.base import Evaluation, Verdict
>>> log = EvaluationLog(MemoryLines())
>>> view = log.pinned(base='B', heads={'a': 'A1'})
>>> _ = view.record(Evaluation(frozenset('a'), Verdict.PASS))
>>> log.pins is None, len(log), len(view)
(True, 1, 1)
>>> len(log.pinned(base='B', heads={'a': 'A2'}))
0
```

#### record(evaluation)

Append `evaluation` and return it.

`at` is stamped if absent, and so are the pinned commits: a row that
does not say what it was run against cannot be told apart from one
about a branch that has since been rewritten.

* **Return type:**
  [`Evaluation`](_autosummary/mergeset.base.html.md#mergeset.base.Evaluation)

#### *property* rows *: [List](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.List)[[Evaluation](_autosummary/mergeset.base.html.md#mergeset.base.Evaluation)]*

Every row in the log, matching the pins or not, in log order.

#### *property* stale *: [List](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.List)[[Evaluation](_autosummary/mergeset.base.html.md#mergeset.base.Evaluation)]*

Rows evaluated against other commits, or by another validator.

Not wrong — about a different question — so kept, and not matched.

#### *property* trust_unpinned *: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*

Whether rows recording no commits count once the log is pinned.

#### *property* unpinned *: [List](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.List)[[Evaluation](_autosummary/mergeset.base.html.md#mergeset.base.Evaluation)]*

Rows recording too little to match that a pinned log is not counting.

No commits (written before #23), or no validator while the pins name
one (written before #32). All of them by default; with
`trust_unpinned`, only those holding a change that is not in play.
Empty when the log is unpinned.

### *class* mergeset.log.JsonlLines(path)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Append-only sequence of JSON objects backed by one file.

The default persistence seam of [`EvaluationLog`](_autosummary/mergeset.log.html.md#mergeset.log.EvaluationLog). Any object with
`append(jdict)` and `__iter__() -> Iterable[jdict]` can replace it (an
in-memory list, a `dol` store, a database table).

```pycon
>>> import tempfile, os
>>> path = os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(), 'x.jsonl')
>>> lines = JsonlLines(path)
>>> lines.append({'a': 1}); lines.append({'a': 2})
>>> [d['a'] for d in lines]
[1, 2]
```

Append one record, flushing immediately (crash-safe enough).

What the log already knows about a set, without re-evaluating it.

#### exact *: [Evaluation](_autosummary/mergeset.base.html.md#mergeset.base.Evaluation) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)* *= None*

#### witness *: [frozenset](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#frozenset) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)* *= None*

### *class* mergeset.log.MemoryLines(iterable=(),)

Bases: [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)

#### append(jdict)

Append object to the end of the list.

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### *class* mergeset.log.Pins(base, heads, validator=None, resolver=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

What a question is about: the base, each change’s head sha, the validator.

A row *matches* when it was merged onto the same base and every change it
holds is in play with the same head. A row holding a change that is not in
play does not match: its head for that change is unchecked, and such a row
would otherwise surface as an “established” set recommending a change
nobody asked about, or as a monotonicity violation between two heads of it.

```pycon
>>> from mergeset.base import Evaluation, Verdict
>>> pins = Pins('B', {'a': 'A1', 'b': 'B1'})
>>> row = Evaluation(frozenset('ab'), Verdict.PASS,
...                  base_sha='B', heads={'a': 'A1', 'b': 'B1'})
>>> pins.matches(row)
True
>>> pins.matches(replace(row, heads={'a': 'A0', 'b': 'B1'}))  # a rewritten
False
>>> pins.matches(replace(row, base_sha='B0'))                 # base moved
False
>>> Pins('B', {'a': 'A1'}).matches(row)          # b is not in play
False
```

With a `validator` fingerprint, a row must also have been judged by that
validator. A row recording none (written before i2mint/mergeset#32) is not
refuted, only incomplete: see [`EvaluationLog.unpinned`](_autosummary/mergeset.log.html.md#mergeset.log.EvaluationLog.unpinned).

```pycon
>>> pins = Pins('B', {'a': 'A1', 'b': 'B1'}, validator='command:1')
>>> pins.matches(replace(row, validator='command:1'))
True
>>> pins.refutes(replace(row, validator='command:2'))   # the command changed
True
>>> pins.matches(row), pins.refutes(row)                # recorded no validator
(False, False)
```

#### complete(evaluation)

True iff `evaluation` records everything these pins compare.

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

#### matches(evaluation)

True iff `evaluation` was run against these commits, by this validator.

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

#### refutes(evaluation)

True iff what `evaluation` records shows it answers another question.

Other commits, or another validator. A row that records too little to
tell is not refuted – it is incomplete (see [`complete()`](_autosummary/mergeset.log.html.md#mergeset.log.Pins.complete)).

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

#### resolver *: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)* *= None*

`'none'` (conflicts stand), or the
resolver’s fingerprint (i2mint/mergeset#34). `None` compares none.

* **Type:**
  How the question’s sets are merged

#### stamp(evaluation)

`evaluation` pinned to these commits and validator, where it is not.

Pins naming no validator stamp [`UNKNOWN_FINGERPRINT`](_autosummary/mergeset.base.html.md#mergeset.base.UNKNOWN_FINGERPRINT),
never nothing: a row recording no validator reads as written before
validators were recorded, and `trust_unpinned` would adopt it.

* **Return type:**
  [`Evaluation`](_autosummary/mergeset.base.html.md#mergeset.base.Evaluation)

#### validator *: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)* *= None*

Fingerprint of the validator the question is asked of (`'unknown'`
when it cannot say what it runs). `None` compares no validator at all.

### *class* mergeset.log.StoreLines(store, key)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Lines backed by one key of a `MutableMapping` — the non-file backend.

[`JsonlLines`](_autosummary/mergeset.log.html.md#mergeset.log.JsonlLines) is the right thing over a filesystem: `open(..., 'a')`
is a true append. An object store has no append, so this reads, concatenates
and writes back. That is honest about the cost rather than pretending, and it
is what lets the evaluation log — the source of truth — reach S3 through the
same seam as everything else.

A missing key reads as empty rather than raising, so a first run works.

```pycon
>>> backing = {}
>>> lines = StoreLines(backing, 'run.jsonl')
>>> list(lines)
[]
>>> lines.append({'a': 1}); lines.append({'a': 2})
>>> [d['a'] for d in lines]
[1, 2]
>>> backing['run.jsonl']
'{"a": 1}\n{"a": 2}\n'
```

#### append(jdict)

Append one record by rewriting the value (no append primitive here).

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### mergeset.log.sets_evaluated(log)

Yield `(sorted ids, verdict)` for every row — handy for reports.

* **Return type:**
  [`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterable)[[`Tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Tuple)[[`Tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Tuple)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis)], [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]


# _autosummary/mergeset.oracle.html.md

# mergeset.oracle

The oracle: turn a change set into a verdict by merging, then validating.

This is the expensive seam of the whole package, and it is assembled from two
injected pieces — a *merge function* and a *validation function* — so that every
part of it can be replaced without touching the search.

The default merge is a plain sequential `git merge` in a throwaway worktree:
any textual conflict is a failure, and the conflicting files are recorded. An
**AI-assisted** mode is available (and is intended as the default when running
inside a Claude Code subagent): on a textual conflict a resolver may attempt a
fix under a strict policy — mechanical conflicts only, never a semantic guess —
and the result is *flagged* as “mergeable with assisted resolution” with the
resolution diff saved. It is never silently reported as a clean merge.

### Module Attributes

| [`RESOLVED_REF_PREFIX`](_autosummary/mergeset.oracle.html.md#mergeset.oracle.RESOLVED_REF_PREFIX)       | Where a resolved merge commit is kept reachable (`<prefix><sha>`), so a log that outlives `git gc`'s grace period can still be confirmed.   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`Resolver`](_autosummary/mergeset.oracle.html.md#mergeset.oracle.Resolver)                  | `(worktree, conflicting_files) -> (resolved?, diff)`.                                                                                       |
| [`RESOLVER_FINGERPRINT_ATTR`](_autosummary/mergeset.oracle.html.md#mergeset.oracle.RESOLVER_FINGERPRINT_ATTR) | The attribute a resolver carries to say how it resolves (i2mint/mergeset#34).                                                               |

### Functions

| [`claude_code_resolver`](_autosummary/mergeset.oracle.html.md#mergeset.oracle.claude_code_resolver)(\*[, timeout, command])   | Resolve conflicts with a Claude Code subagent, under a strict policy.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`git_oracle`](_autosummary/mergeset.oracle.html.md#mergeset.oracle.git_oracle)(repo, base, changes, \*[, ...])     | Build the evaluator: merge the set onto `base`, then validate the tree. |
| [`merge_order`](_autosummary/mergeset.oracle.html.md#mergeset.oracle.merge_order)(subset, changes)                   | A deterministic merge order for a change set.                           |
| [`resolver_fingerprint_of`](_autosummary/mergeset.oracle.html.md#mergeset.oracle.resolver_fingerprint_of)(resolver)              | How `resolver` resolves conflicts, as the string a log row records.     |

### mergeset.oracle.RESOLVED_REF_PREFIX *= 'refs/mergeset/resolved/'*

Where a resolved merge commit is kept reachable (`<prefix><sha>`), so a
log that outlives `git gc`’s grace period can still be confirmed.

### mergeset.oracle.Resolver

alias of `Callable`[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]], `Tuple`[[`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]

### mergeset.oracle.claude_code_resolver(, timeout=300.0, command='claude')

Resolve conflicts with a Claude Code subagent, under a strict policy.

The policy is in the prompt and is deliberately narrow: mechanical conflicts
only (import blocks, changelog entries, adjacent independent edits, lockfile
regeneration), and an explicit refusal whenever the resolution requires
guessing intent. Anything it does resolve is flagged and its diff kept.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]], [`Tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Tuple)[[`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]

### mergeset.oracle.git_oracle(repo, base, changes, , validate=None, resolver=None, resolution=None, depends_on=None, reuse_worktree=None, worktree_root=None, keep_worktrees=False, on_event=None)

Build the evaluator: merge the set onto `base`, then validate the tree.

* **Parameters:**
  * **repo** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Path to the git repository (worktrees are created off it).
  * **base** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – The commit everything is merged onto.
  * **changes** ([`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterable)[[`Change`](_autosummary/mergeset.base.html.md#mergeset.base.Change)]) – The changes in play; only their ids are passed around later.
  * **validate** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`ValidationOutcome`](_autosummary/mergeset.base.html.md#mergeset.base.ValidationOutcome)]]) – `worktree -> ValidationOutcome`. Defaults to a fail-fast
    pytest run; see [`mergeset.validation`](_autosummary/mergeset.validation.html.md#module-mergeset.validation) for the alternatives.
  * **resolver** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]], [`Tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Tuple)[[`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]]) – Optional AI-assisted conflict resolver. When given, a textual
    conflict is offered to it; a success is recorded with
    `merge.assisted = True`, the diff kept, and the resolved merge
    commit kept as `merge.resolved_commit`.
  * **resolution** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`frozenset`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#frozenset)], [`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`MergeOutcome`](_autosummary/mergeset.base.html.md#mergeset.base.MergeOutcome)]]]) – `subset -> MergeOutcome` of an earlier assisted
    resolution of that set, or `None` – the alternative to
    `resolver` for a deeper tier (i2mint/mergeset#30). A conflicting
    set is then not resolved again: the recorded commit is checked out,
    once it is shown to hold the base and every head, so every tier
    validates the very tree the first one did and the resolver is paid
    once. A conflict with no usable recorded resolution is an
    `ERROR`, never a guess.
  * **depends_on** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]) – `child -> parent` for stacked changes. Only the *tips* of
    a set are merged, because merging a tip already brings its
    ancestors; merging them explicitly is wasted work and perturbs the
    merge order for no reason.
  * **reuse_worktree** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – An existing worktree to check every candidate merge out
    into, instead of a fresh one per evaluation. This is what makes an
    expensive per-tree setup (dependency install, build cache)
    amortizable across the whole run.
  * **worktree_root** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – Where throwaway worktrees go. Default: a temp dir.
  * **keep_worktrees** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Keep them for inspection (they add up fast).
  * **on_event** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)], [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)]]) – `(event, payload)` progress callback.
* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`frozenset`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#frozenset)], [`Evaluation`](_autosummary/mergeset.base.html.md#mergeset.base.Evaluation)]
* **Returns:**
  `evaluate(subset) -> Evaluation`. Wrap it in
  `EvaluationLog.caching` before handing it to the solver.

### mergeset.oracle.merge_order(subset, changes)

A deterministic merge order for a change set.

Order should not matter when merges are clean; when it does, the run is
recorded with the order that was used so the result stays reproducible.
Stacked changes are merged parent-first; otherwise smallest-first, which
surfaces the cheap conflicts early.

* **Return type:**
  [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

```pycon
>>> merge_order(frozenset({'b', 'a'}), {})
['a', 'b']
```

### mergeset.oracle.resolver_fingerprint_of(resolver)

How `resolver` resolves conflicts, as the string a log row records.

A row whose outcome a resolver decided (an assisted merge, or a conflict
left standing) answers only runs that resolve the same way: see
[`mergeset.base.Evaluation.merge_dependent`](_autosummary/mergeset.base.html.md#mergeset.base.Evaluation.merge_dependent). `None` resolves
nothing ([`NO_RESOLVER`](_autosummary/mergeset.base.html.md#mergeset.base.NO_RESOLVER)); a resolver that cannot say
how it resolves records [`UNKNOWN_FINGERPRINT`](_autosummary/mergeset.base.html.md#mergeset.base.UNKNOWN_FINGERPRINT), which
matches only other such rows. A user resolver may set
`resolver.resolver_fingerprint = 'my-resolver-v2'`.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

```pycon
>>> resolver_fingerprint_of(None)
'none'
>>> resolver_fingerprint_of(lambda worktree, files: (False, ''))
'unknown'
>>> resolver_fingerprint_of(claude_code_resolver()).startswith('claude-code:')
True
```


# _autosummary/mergeset.report.html.md

# mergeset.report

Rendering an [`Analysis`](_autosummary/mergeset.analysis.html.md#mergeset.analysis.Analysis) for humans.

Two renderers: a Markdown report meant to be read in a terminal or a PR comment,
and a single self-contained HTML file (no build step, no CDN) meant to be opened
and poked at. Both are pure functions of the analysis, which is itself derived
from the evaluation log — so a report can always be regenerated without
re-running anything expensive.

### Module Attributes

| [`REPORT_FORMATS`](_autosummary/mergeset.report.html.md#mergeset.report.REPORT_FORMATS)   | format name -> (key suffix, is it bytes).   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------|

| [`html_report`](_autosummary/mergeset.report.html.md#mergeset.report.html_report)(analysis, \*[, title])                 | Render the analysis as one self-contained HTML file.                     |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`markdown_report`](_autosummary/mergeset.report.html.md#mergeset.report.markdown_report)(analysis, \*[, title])             | Render the analysis as Markdown.                                         |
| [`pdf_report`](_autosummary/mergeset.report.html.md#mergeset.report.pdf_report)(analysis, \*[, title])                  | Render the analysis as a PDF, for the reader who wants one file to keep. |
| [`stage_breakdown`](_autosummary/mergeset.report.html.md#mergeset.report.stage_breakdown)(record)                            | Where an evaluation's time went, stage by stage; `''` if not recorded.   |
| [`write_reports`](_autosummary/mergeset.report.html.md#mergeset.report.write_reports)(analysis, \*[, title, formats, ...]) | Render a run's reports into the artifact store; return `{format: key}`.  |

  What `write_reports` can produce

### mergeset.report.html_report(analysis, , title='mergeset')

Render the analysis as one self-contained HTML file.

No build step, no CDN, no network: a single file that can be opened from
disk or attached to an issue. It draws the conflict graph (nodes = changes,
edges = conflicts, textual vs validation distinguished), the maximal sets,
and the evaluation timeline.

* **Return type:**

Render the analysis as Markdown.

Sections, in the order a reader actually wants them: what to merge, what

### mergeset.report.pdf_report(analysis, , title='mergeset report')

Render the analysis as a PDF, for the reader who wants one file to keep.

Rendered from the **Markdown**, not the HTML. The HTML report draws its
conflict graph and tables from an embedded JSON blob at load time, so a
print pipeline that does not execute JavaScript would render a blank page —
a PDF that looks fine until someone opens it. The Markdown is static, so
what is printed is what the report says.

Needs `pdfdol`; `pip install 'mergeset[pdf]'`. The error says so rather
than surfacing an ImportError from three frames down.

* **Return type:**
  [`bytes`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#bytes)

### mergeset.report.stage_breakdown(record)

Where an evaluation’s time went, stage by stage; `''` if not recorded.

The actionable version of a duration: “33 s of its 51 s installing
dependencies” says what to fix, “51 s” does not. The remainder of the
total – merging, worktree setup – is shown as `other`.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

```pycon
>>> from mergeset.base import StageRun, ValidationOutcome, Verdict
>>> v = ValidationOutcome(True, duration=48.5, stages=[
...     StageRun('setup', 33.0, 0), StageRun('build', 9.0, 0),
...     StageRun('test', 6.5, 0)])
>>> stage_breakdown(Evaluation(frozenset('a'), Verdict.PASS,
...                            validation=v, duration=49.0))
'setup 33.0 · build 9.0 · test 6.5 · other 0.5'
>>> v = ValidationOutcome(True, stages=[StageRun('setup', skipped=True),
...                                     StageRun('test', 6.0, 0)])
>>> stage_breakdown(Evaluation(frozenset('a'), Verdict.PASS, validation=v,
...                            duration=6.0))
'setup skipped · test 6.0'
```

### mergeset.report.write_reports(analysis, , title='mergeset report', formats=('markdown', 'html'), key=None, reports=None, binary_reports=None, rootdir=None)

Render a run’s reports into the artifact store; return `{format: key}`.

The single place that knows how a run’s reports are named and where they
go, so the CLI, the library and any future surface cannot drift apart on it.

`key` defaults to `<repo-slug>/<timestamp>` — per run, so re-analysing a
repository never overwrites the answer you are comparing against. Nothing is
written into the analysed repository, ever: see [`mergeset.storage`](_autosummary/mergeset.storage.html.md#module-mergeset.storage).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

```pycon
>>> from mergeset.analysis import Analysis
>>> a = Analysis(repo='/x/y/proj', base='main', base_sha='0'*40, changes=[])
>>> text, binary = {}, {}
>>> written = write_reports(a, key='run-1', reports=text, binary_reports=binary)
>>> sorted(written)
['html', 'markdown']
>>> sorted(text)
['run-1/REPORT.md', 'run-1/report.html']
```


# _autosummary/mergeset.skills.html.md

# mergeset.skills

The agent skill that ships inside the package, and how to install it.

`mergeset` bundles an [Agent Skill](https://agentskills.io) — the operating
instructions an AI agent needs to drive this tool well: which oracle to ask
first, what a report does *not* mean, and what must never be committed. It is
real files inside the installed package, so `pip install mergeset` already
delivers it:

```default
>>> (skills_dir() / 'mergeset' / 'SKILL.md').is_file()
True
```

Agent hosts do not read the package, though — they read their own skills
directory. [`install_skills()`](_autosummary/mergeset.skills.html.md#mergeset.skills.install_skills) bridges the two:

```bash
mergeset install-skills                            # -> ~/.claude/skills
mergeset install-skills --target ~/.agents/skills  # any host's directory
```

The default is a symlink, so `pip install -U mergeset` updates the installed
skill too. Every part is one keyword argument away from being replaced: where
the skills come from (`skills_root`), where they go (`target`), and whether
the link is a symlink or a copy (`link`).

### Module Attributes

| [`DEFAULT_TARGET`](_autosummary/mergeset.skills.html.md#mergeset.skills.DEFAULT_TARGET)   | Where an agent host looks by default.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------|

### Functions

| [`bundled_skills`](_autosummary/mergeset.skills.html.md#mergeset.skills.bundled_skills)([skills_root])                    | Yield the directory of every bundled skill (each holding a `SKILL.md`).   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`install_skills`](_autosummary/mergeset.skills.html.md#mergeset.skills.install_skills)([target, skills_root, link, ...]) | Put the bundled skills where an agent host will find them.                |
| [`skills_dir`](_autosummary/mergeset.skills.html.md#mergeset.skills.skills_dir)()                                     | The directory of skills bundled inside the installed package.             |

### mergeset.skills.DEFAULT_TARGET *= '~/.claude/skills'*

Where an agent host looks by default. Overridden per call, or per host.

### mergeset.skills.bundled_skills(skills_root=None)

Yield the directory of every bundled skill (each holding a `SKILL.md`).

`skills_root` is resolved, so a relative one still yields links that work
from anywhere.

* **Return type:**
  [`Iterator`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterator)[[`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)]

```pycon
>>> [p.name for p in bundled_skills()]
['mergeset']
```

### mergeset.skills.install_skills(target='~/.claude/skills', , skills_root=None, link=True, overwrite=False)

Put the bundled skills where an agent host will find them.

Returns the destination path of every skill installed. A destination that
already holds a skill is left alone, so re-running is safe and an edited
skill is never silently replaced — and anything *else* sitting in the way
(a file, a stale broken link) raises rather than being reported as fine.

`overwrite=True` is the escape hatch, and it is not gentle: it deletes
whatever is at the destination, including a directory someone kept notes in.

* **Return type:**
  [`List`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.List)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

```pycon
>>> import tempfile
>>> dest = tempfile.mkdtemp()
>>> installed = install_skills(dest)
>>> [Path(p).name for p in installed]
['mergeset']
>>> Path(installed[0], 'SKILL.md').read_text().startswith('---')
True
>>> install_skills(dest)          # already there, nothing to do
[]
```

### mergeset.skills.skills_dir()

The directory of skills bundled inside the installed package.

* **Return type:**
  [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)

```pycon
>>> skills_dir().name
'skills'
```


# _autosummary/mergeset.solve.html.md

# mergeset.solve

The search: from expensive yes/no evaluations to maximal good sets.

Vocabulary (standard in the MUS/MSS literature):

- a **conflict** is a minimal *bad* set (an MUS): remove any member and it stops
  being bad;
- a **maximal good set** is a good set that cannot be grown (an MSS);
- by Reiter’s hitting-set duality, the complement of a maximal good set is
  exactly a minimal hitting set of the conflicts.

So the loop is: propose the complement of the cheapest minimal hitting set of
the conflicts known so far; evaluate it; if it fails, shrink the failure to a
new conflict (QuickXplain) and propose again; if it passes, it is a maximal good
set — record it and ask for the next-cheapest hitting set.

Nothing here knows about git. The only thing it needs is `evaluate(subset) ->
Evaluation`, which is why the whole package is testable without a repository.

### Functions

| [`combine_components`](_autosummary/mergeset.solve.html.md#mergeset.solve.combine_components)(per_component)                  | Cartesian-combine per-component maximal sets into global ones.             |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`find_maximal_good_sets`](_autosummary/mergeset.solve.html.md#mergeset.solve.find_maximal_good_sets)(changes, evaluate, \*)      | Enumerate maximal good subsets of `changes`, cheapest-dropped first.       |
| [`independent_components`](_autosummary/mergeset.solve.html.md#mergeset.solve.independent_components)(changes, files_of)          | Split changes into groups that cannot possibly interact via files.         |
| [`minimal_hitting_sets`](_autosummary/mergeset.solve.html.md#mergeset.solve.minimal_hitting_sets)(conflicts, \*[, weight, ...]) | Yield minimal hitting sets of `conflicts`, cheapest total weight first.    |
| [`quickxplain`](_autosummary/mergeset.solve.html.md#mergeset.solve.quickxplain)(evaluate, candidates, \*[, ...])       | Shrink a known-bad set to one minimal conflict, in O(k log n) evaluations. |
| [`shrink_linear`](_autosummary/mergeset.solve.html.md#mergeset.solve.shrink_linear)(evaluate, candidates, \*[, ...])     | One-at-a-time conflict shrinking: `n` evaluations, dead simple.            |

### Classes

| [`SearchState`](_autosummary/mergeset.solve.html.md#mergeset.solve.SearchState)([conflicts, maximal_good_sets, ...])   | Everything the search accumulated.   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------|

### *class* mergeset.solve.SearchState(conflicts=<factory>, maximal_good_sets=<factory>, evaluations=0, elapsed=0.0, exhausted=False, stopped_because='', error='')

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Everything the search accumulated. Derived entirely from the log.

#### add_conflict(conflict)

Add `conflict`, keeping the list free of non-minimal members.

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

#### error *: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)* *= ''*

Set when an evaluation could not be performed at all. The results below
are not wrong so much as unfinished, and must not be presented as an
answer: “we could not run the experiment” is not “the experiment failed”.

### mergeset.solve.combine_components(per_component)

Cartesian-combine per-component maximal sets into global ones.

* **Return type:**
  [`List`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.List)[[`frozenset`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#frozenset)]

```pycon
>>> [set_key(s) for s in combine_components([[frozenset('a')], [frozenset('c')]])]
[('a', 'c')]
```

### mergeset.solve.find_maximal_good_sets(changes, evaluate, \*, known_conflicts=(), depends_on=None, weight=None, max_evaluations=None, max_seconds=None, max_sets=None, shrink=<function quickxplain>, suspects=None, on_event=None)

Enumerate maximal good subsets of `changes`, cheapest-dropped first.

* **Parameters:**
  * **changes** ([`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterable)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – The change ids in play.
  * **evaluate** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`frozenset`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#frozenset)], [`Evaluation`](_autosummary/mergeset.base.html.md#mergeset.base.Evaluation)]) – The (cached, log-backed) oracle.
  * **known_conflicts** ([`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterable)[[`frozenset`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#frozenset)]) – Conflicts already known for free — e.g. textual
    `git merge-tree` conflicts and singletons whose own CI is red.
    These cost zero evaluations and prune enormously.
  * **depends_on** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]) – `child -> parent` for stacked changes. When given, only
    downward-closed sets are ever proposed (a change is never evaluated
    without the changes it is built on) and dropping a change implicitly
    drops everything stacked on it. See [`mergeset.stacks`](_autosummary/mergeset.stacks.html.md#module-mergeset.stacks).
  * **weight** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]]) – `id -> cost of dropping it`. Higher means “keep me”.
  * **max_evaluations** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]) – Budgets. Whichever trips first
    stops the search; partial results are always returned.
  * **max_seconds** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]) – Budgets. Whichever trips first
    stops the search; partial results are always returned.
  * **max_sets** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]) – Budgets. Whichever trips first
    stops the search; partial results are always returned.
  * **shrink** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`frozenset`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#frozenset)]) – Conflict-minimization strategy ([`quickxplain()`](_autosummary/mergeset.solve.html.md#mergeset.solve.quickxplain) by default).
  * **suspects** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`Evaluation`](_autosummary/mergeset.base.html.md#mergeset.base.Evaluation), [`frozenset`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#frozenset)], [`frozenset`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#frozenset)]]) – `(failed evaluation, the set) -> the changes it implicates`.
    Lets the search shrink within the implicated changes instead of
    halving the whole set. A wrong hint costs one wasted check and then
    falls back; see [`mergeset.attribution`](_autosummary/mergeset.attribution.html.md#module-mergeset.attribution).
  * **on_event** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)], [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)]]) – `(event_name, payload)` progress callback.
* **Return type:**
  [`SearchState`](_autosummary/mergeset.solve.html.md#mergeset.solve.SearchState)
* **Returns:**
  A [`SearchState`](_autosummary/mergeset.solve.html.md#mergeset.solve.SearchState). `exhausted` says whether the answer is
  complete or merely the best found within budget.

```pycon
>>> bad = [{'a', 'c'}]
>>> def ev(s):
...     ok = not any(p <= set(s) for p in bad)
...     return Evaluation(s, Verdict.PASS if ok else Verdict.FAIL)
>>> state = find_maximal_good_sets(['a', 'b', 'c'], ev)
>>> [set_key(s) for s in state.maximal_good_sets]
[('a', 'b'), ('b', 'c')]
>>> [set_key(c) for c in state.conflicts]
[('a', 'c')]
```

### mergeset.solve.independent_components(changes, files_of)

Split changes into groups that cannot possibly interact via files.

Two changes touching disjoint file sets cannot conflict textually, and (as a
working assumption worth stating out loud) rarely conflict semantically.
Connected components of the file-overlap graph are therefore independent
subproblems: solve each separately and combine the answers freely, which
turns one `2**n` search into several much smaller ones.

* **Return type:**
  [`List`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.List)[[`frozenset`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#frozenset)]

```pycon
>>> files = {'a': ['x.py'], 'b': ['x.py'], 'c': ['y.py']}
>>> [set_key(g) for g in independent_components(files, files.get)]
[('a', 'b'), ('c',)]
```

### mergeset.solve.minimal_hitting_sets(conflicts, , weight=None, limit=None)

Yield minimal hitting sets of `conflicts`, cheapest total weight first.

A hitting set touches every conflict; its complement is therefore a set with
no known conflict inside it. Enumerating hitting sets cheapest-first means
the solver proposes dropping the *least valuable* changes first.

* **Return type:**
  [`Iterator`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterator)[[`frozenset`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#frozenset)]

```pycon
>>> hs = minimal_hitting_sets([frozenset({'a', 'b'}), frozenset({'b', 'c'})])
>>> [sorted(h) for h in itertools.islice(hs, 3)]
[['b'], ['a', 'c']]
```

### mergeset.solve.quickxplain(evaluate, candidates, , background=frozenset({}))

Shrink a known-bad set to one minimal conflict, in O(k log n) evaluations.

Junker’s QuickXplain: recursive halving that costs `O(k log(n/k))`
evaluations for a conflict of size `k` among `n` candidates, rather than
the `O(n)` of naive one-at-a-time removal.

* **Parameters:**
  * **evaluate** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`frozenset`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#frozenset)], [`Evaluation`](_autosummary/mergeset.base.html.md#mergeset.base.Evaluation)]) – The (cached) oracle.
  * **candidates** ([`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – Members that may be part of the conflict.
  * **background** ([`frozenset`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#frozenset)) – Members always present and assumed not, on their own, bad.
* **Return type:**
  [`frozenset`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#frozenset)
* **Returns:**
  A minimal subset `C` of `candidates` with `background | C` bad.

```pycon
>>> bad_pairs = [{'a', 'c'}]
>>> def ev(s):
...     ok = not any(p <= set(s) for p in bad_pairs)
...     return Evaluation(s, Verdict.PASS if ok else Verdict.FAIL)
>>> sorted(quickxplain(ev, ['a', 'b', 'c', 'd']))
['a', 'c']
```

### mergeset.solve.shrink_linear(evaluate, candidates, , background=frozenset({}))

One-at-a-time conflict shrinking: `n` evaluations, dead simple.

Kept because it is the obviously-correct reference that
[`quickxplain()`](_autosummary/mergeset.solve.html.md#mergeset.solve.quickxplain) is checked against, and because for very small `n` it
is not actually slower.

* **Return type:**
  [`frozenset`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#frozenset)


# _autosummary/mergeset.sources.html.md

# mergeset.sources

Change sources: where the candidate changes come from.

A **source** is any callable returning an iterable of [`Change`](_autosummary/mergeset.base.html.md#mergeset.base.Change).
Branches, pull requests and explicit commit lists are just different sources of
the same thing — a `base..head` range — which is why the rest of the package
never mentions the word “PR”.

PR sources carry the extra metadata that only a forge knows (author, title, CI
status, base branch, draft flag, stack relationships); it rides along in
`Change.meta` and is used for weighting and for the report, never by the
solver.

### Module Attributes

| [`PR_FIELDS`](_autosummary/mergeset.sources.html.md#mergeset.sources.PR_FIELDS)   | Fields worth asking `gh` for; anything else is noise in the report.   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Functions

| [`branch_changes`](_autosummary/mergeset.sources.html.md#mergeset.sources.branch_changes)(repo, branches, \*[, base, prefix])   | Changes from local or remote branches.                                |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`check_gh_capability`](_autosummary/mergeset.sources.html.md#mergeset.sources.check_gh_capability)()                                | Raise a fixable error if the GitHub CLI is unusable.                  |
| [`commit_changes`](_autosummary/mergeset.sources.html.md#mergeset.sources.commit_changes)(repo, commits, \*[, base])            | Changes from an explicit list of commit-ishes, one change per commit. |
| [`detect_stacks`](_autosummary/mergeset.sources.html.md#mergeset.sources.detect_stacks)(changes)                               | Map change id -> the change id it is stacked on, for PR stacks.       |
| [`fetch_pull_requests`](_autosummary/mergeset.sources.html.md#mergeset.sources.fetch_pull_requests)(repo_spec, \*[, author, ...])    | Raw `gh pr list` records for `repo_spec` (`owner/name`).              |
| [`local_branch_names`](_autosummary/mergeset.sources.html.md#mergeset.sources.local_branch_names)(repo, \*[, pattern, exclude])     | Local branch names, optionally filtered by a glob `pattern`.          |
| [`pr_changes`](_autosummary/mergeset.sources.html.md#mergeset.sources.pr_changes)(repo, pull_requests, \*[, base, ...])     | Turn `gh pr list` records into changes.                               |
| [`size_weight`](_autosummary/mergeset.sources.html.md#mergeset.sources.size_weight)(repo, change)                            | Default weight: how much it costs to drop this change.                |

### mergeset.sources.detect_stacks(changes)

Map change id -> the change id it is stacked on, for PR stacks.

A PR whose base ref is another candidate’s head ref is *stacked*: only
prefixes of the chain make sense as a merge set, because the child contains
the parent. Recorded so the report can say so and the solver can be told.

* **Return type:**
  [`Dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

```pycon
>>> a = Change(id='pr1', head='origin/a', base='origin/main', source='pr',
...            meta={'head_ref': 'a', 'base_ref': 'main'})
>>> b = Change(id='pr2', head='origin/b', base='origin/a', source='pr',
...            meta={'head_ref': 'b', 'base_ref': 'a'})
>>> detect_stacks([a, b])
{'pr2': 'pr1'}
```
