Turn `gh pr list` records into changes.

* **Parameters:**
  * **repo** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Local clone the refs live in.
  * **pull_requests** ([`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterable)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]) – Records as produced by [`fetch_pull_requests()`](_autosummary/mergeset.sources.html.md#mergeset.sources.fetch_pull_requests).
  * **base** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – Override base for every change. Default: each PR’s own base ref,
    which is what makes stacked PRs visible rather than silently wrong.
  * **ref_of** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)], [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]) – How to name a PR’s head ref locally. Default `origin/<headRef>`.
* **Return type:**
  [`Iterator`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Iterator)[[`Change`](_autosummary/mergeset.base.html.md#mergeset.base.Change)]

### mergeset.sources.size_weight(repo, change)

Default weight: how much it costs to drop this change.

Bigger changes are worth more (dropping a 900-line PR wastes more work than
dropping a typo fix), so the weighted hitting set prefers to drop the small
ones. `log`-shaped so one huge branch does not dominate everything.

Override with any `Change -> float`; PR metadata (priority labels,
author, age) is right there in `change.meta` for the taking.

* **Return type:**
  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)


# _autosummary/mergeset.stacks.html.md

# mergeset.stacks

Stacked changes: when the candidates are not independent.

A pull request opened against another pull request’s branch already *contains*
it. That single fact breaks the assumption that any subset of the candidates is
a meaningful thing to evaluate, and it breaks it in three places at once:

- **Validity.** Asking for `{616}` when 616 is stacked on 604 on 587 really
  means `{587, 604, 616}`. A valid set must be **downward-closed** under the
  parent relation. Note “downward-closed in a forest”, not “a prefix of a
  chain”: stacks branch, so two changes can be siblings on the same parent.
- **Cost.** Merging a stack’s tip brings every ancestor with it, so merging the
  ancestors explicitly is wasted work and can perturb merge order. Reduce a set
  to its **tips** before merging.
- **Weight.** Dropping a change drops its whole descendant cone. Weighting
  changes independently lets a hitting set cheerfully discard thousands of lines
  while believing it discarded one small PR.

Discovering the relation is [`mergeset.sources.detect_stacks()`](_autosummary/mergeset.sources.html.md#mergeset.sources.detect_stacks); acting on it
is here. The dependency map is always `child -> parent`.

### Module Attributes

| [`Dependencies`](_autosummary/mergeset.stacks.html.md#mergeset.stacks.Dependencies)   | `child -> parent`.   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------|

### Functions

| [`ancestors`](_autosummary/mergeset.stacks.html.md#mergeset.stacks.ancestors)(change, parents)             | Every change `change` is stacked on, transitively.                          |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`close_down`](_autosummary/mergeset.stacks.html.md#mergeset.stacks.close_down)(subset, parents)            | Add every ancestor, so the set becomes a valid thing to ask for.            |
| [`close_up`](_autosummary/mergeset.stacks.html.md#mergeset.stacks.close_up)(subset, parents)              | Add every descendant — what dropping these changes actually costs.          |
| [`cone_weights`](_autosummary/mergeset.stacks.html.md#mergeset.stacks.cone_weights)(weights, parents)         | Re-weight each change by the cost of dropping its whole descendant cone.    |
| [`count_closed_subsets`](_autosummary/mergeset.stacks.html.md#mergeset.stacks.count_closed_subsets)(parents, changes) | How many downward-closed subsets exist — the size of the real search space. |
| [`descendants`](_autosummary/mergeset.stacks.html.md#mergeset.stacks.descendants)(change, parents)           | Every change stacked on `change`, transitively — its *cone*.                |
| [`largest_closed_subset`](_autosummary/mergeset.stacks.html.md#mergeset.stacks.largest_closed_subset)(subset, parents) | Drop members whose ancestors are missing — the set you can actually merge.  |
| [`stack_roots`](_autosummary/mergeset.stacks.html.md#mergeset.stacks.stack_roots)(parents, changes)          | Group changes into stacks (connected components of the parent relation).    |
| [`tips`](_autosummary/mergeset.stacks.html.md#mergeset.stacks.tips)(subset, parents)                  | The members of `subset` that nothing else in `subset` is stacked on.        |

### mergeset.stacks.Dependencies

`child -> parent`. A change absent from the mapping has no parent.

alias of [`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### mergeset.stacks.ancestors(change, parents)

Every change `change` is stacked on, transitively.

* **Return type:**
  [`frozenset`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#frozenset)

```pycon
>>> set_key(ancestors('c', {'c': 'b', 'b': 'a'}))
('a', 'b')
```

### mergeset.stacks.close_down(subset, parents)

Add every ancestor, so the set becomes a valid thing to ask for.

* **Return type:**
  [`frozenset`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#frozenset)

```pycon
>>> set_key(close_down({'c'}, {'c': 'b', 'b': 'a'}))
('a', 'b', 'c')
```

### mergeset.stacks.close_up(subset, parents)

Add every descendant — what dropping these changes actually costs.

* **Return type:**
  [`frozenset`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#frozenset)

```pycon
>>> set_key(close_up({'a'}, {'c': 'b', 'b': 'a'}))
('a', 'b', 'c')
```

### mergeset.stacks.cone_weights(weights, parents)

Re-weight each change by the cost of dropping its whole descendant cone.

Dropping a stack’s root drops the stack. The hitting set has to know that,
or it will pick the “cheapest” change and take eight thousand lines with it.

* **Return type:**
  [`Dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]

```pycon
>>> cone_weights({'a': 1.0, 'b': 2.0}, {'b': 'a'})
{'a': 3.0, 'b': 2.0}
```

### mergeset.stacks.count_closed_subsets(parents, changes)

How many downward-closed subsets exist — the size of the real search space.

Worth reporting: on a 15-change forest of four stacks this is 576 rather
than 32768, which is the difference between “enumerate carefully” and
“hopeless”.

* **Return type:**
  [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)

```pycon
>>> count_closed_subsets({'b': 'a'}, ['a', 'b'])
3
```

### mergeset.stacks.descendants(change, parents)

Every change stacked on `change`, transitively — its *cone*.

* **Return type:**
  [`frozenset`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#frozenset)

```pycon
>>> set_key(descendants('a', {'c': 'b', 'b': 'a', 'd': 'a'}))
('b', 'c', 'd')
```

### mergeset.stacks.largest_closed_subset(subset, parents)

Drop members whose ancestors are missing — the set you can actually merge.

This is the *other* way to make a set valid, and it is the one the solver
needs: when the search decides to drop a parent, the descendants have to go
too, and no amount of wanting them back changes that.

* **Return type:**
  [`frozenset`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#frozenset)

```pycon
>>> set_key(largest_closed_subset({'b', 'c'}, {'c': 'b', 'b': 'a'}))
()
>>> set_key(largest_closed_subset({'a', 'b', 'd'}, {'c': 'b', 'b': 'a'}))
('a', 'b', 'd')
```

### mergeset.stacks.stack_roots(parents, changes)

Group changes into stacks (connected components of the parent relation).

* **Return type:**
  [`List`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.List)[[`frozenset`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#frozenset)]

```pycon
>>> [set_key(g) for g in stack_roots({'b': 'a', 'd': 'c'}, 'abcde')]
[('a', 'b'), ('c', 'd'), ('e',)]
```

### mergeset.stacks.tips(subset, parents)

The members of `subset` that nothing else in `subset` is stacked on.

Merging these brings the rest along for free.

* **Return type:**
  [`frozenset`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#frozenset)

```pycon
>>> set_key(tips({'a', 'b', 'c'}, {'c': 'b', 'b': 'a'}))
('c',)
>>> set_key(tips({'a', 'b', 'd'}, {'b': 'a', 'd': 'a'}))
('b', 'd')
```


# _autosummary/mergeset.storage.html.md

# mergeset.storage

Where mergeset’s artifacts live, and how code reaches them.

Everything mergeset produces — reports, evaluation logs, raw validation output,
captured failure fixtures — is *derived data*. It has a different lifecycle from
code and, crucially, a different **provenance**: it is captured from whatever
repository was analysed, which is very often private. So none of it belongs in a
repository, and the default location makes sure it never lands in one by
accident:

```default
~/.local/share/mergeset/<kind>/          (%LOCALAPPDATA% on Windows)
```

Four kinds, four sub-stores:

| `reports`     | Rendered analyses — `<name>/REPORT.md`, `<name>/report.html`   |
|---------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
| `evaluations` | The append-only JSONL evaluation logs (the source of truth)    |
| `logs`        | Raw build/test/lint output captured during validation          |
| `fixtures`    | Captured failure output kept as regression tests               |

Each store is a plain [`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping) of `str -> str`,
so business logic never learns where the bytes physically are:

```default
>>> import tempfile
>>> mall = artifact_mall(rootdir=tempfile.mkdtemp())
>>> sorted(mall)
['evaluations', 'fixtures', 'logs', 'reports']
>>> reports = mall['reports']
>>> reports['demo/REPORT.md'] = '# hello'
>>> reports['demo/REPORT.md']
'# hello'
>>> list(reports)
['demo/REPORT.md']
```

The backend is one keyword argument (`store_factory`), so pointing the same
code at S3 is a one-line change and no caller notices:

```default
from s3dol import S3Store
mall = artifact_mall(
    store_factory=lambda kind, root, binary=False: S3Store(bucket, prefix=kind)
)
```

A factory is handed the **kind and the root separately**, never a joined
filesystem path — a backend that has no filesystem must not have to parse one
out, and on Windows a joined path would put backslashes in S3 keys.

The root is overridden by one environment variable, `MERGESET_DATA_DIR` — one
knob for the root, never one per kind.

### Module Attributes

| [`ARTIFACT_KINDS`](_autosummary/mergeset.storage.html.md#mergeset.storage.ARTIFACT_KINDS)   | The kinds of artifact mergeset produces.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------|
| [`StoreFactory`](_autosummary/mergeset.storage.html.md#mergeset.storage.StoreFactory)     | `(kind, rootdir, *, binary) -> store`.     |

### Functions

| [`app_data_rootdir`](_autosummary/mergeset.storage.html.md#mergeset.storage.app_data_rootdir)(\*[, app_name, envvar])           | The artifact root for `app_name`, honouring `$MERGESET_DATA_DIR`.   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`artifact_mall`](_autosummary/mergeset.storage.html.md#mergeset.storage.artifact_mall)(\*[, rootdir, store_factory, ...])   | All the artifact stores, keyed by kind — a *mall*, in `dol` terms.  |
| [`artifact_path`](_autosummary/mergeset.storage.html.md#mergeset.storage.artifact_path)(kind[, key, rootdir, app_name])      | Filesystem path for `kind`/`key` under the *local* artifact root.   |
| [`artifact_store`](_autosummary/mergeset.storage.html.md#mergeset.storage.artifact_store)(kind, \*[, rootdir, ...])           | A store for one kind of artifact — `str` values, or `bytes`.        |
| [`evaluation_lines`](_autosummary/mergeset.storage.html.md#mergeset.storage.evaluation_lines)(repo, \*[, store, rootdir, ...])  | The append-only lines object backing this repo's evaluation log.    |
| [`evaluation_log_path`](_autosummary/mergeset.storage.html.md#mergeset.storage.evaluation_log_path)(repo, \*[, rootdir, app_name]) | Default evaluation-log path for `repo` — in the artifact store.     |
| [`run_key`](_autosummary/mergeset.storage.html.md#mergeset.storage.run_key)(repo, \*[, at])                            | A key naming one run of one repository: `<repo-slug>/<timestamp>`.  |
| [`slash_separated_keys`](_autosummary/mergeset.storage.html.md#mergeset.storage.slash_separated_keys)(store, \*[, sep])             | Make `/` the key separator whatever the platform's is.              |
| [`slugify`](_autosummary/mergeset.storage.html.md#mergeset.storage.slugify)(text, \*[, maxlen])                        | A filesystem-safe key naming a run after its repository.            |

### mergeset.storage.ARTIFACT_KINDS *: [Tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Tuple)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), ...]* *= ('reports', 'evaluations', 'logs', 'fixtures')*

The kinds of artifact mergeset produces. One sub-store each; never write to
the root itself, so a fifth kind costs no migration.

### mergeset.storage.StoreFactory

`(kind, rootdir, *, binary) -> store`.
Kind and root are passed separately on purpose — see the module docstring.
`binary` says whether the values are `bytes` (a PDF) or `str` (a report,
a log, a JSONL line). A backend has to know which; it is not a detail the
caller can paper over.

* **Type:**
  What a `store_factory` must be

alias of `Callable`[[…], [`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)]

### mergeset.storage.app_data_rootdir(, app_name='mergeset', envvar='MERGESET_DATA_DIR')

The artifact root for `app_name`, honouring `$MERGESET_DATA_DIR`.

It is a *root*, not a leaf: artifacts always go in a per-kind subfolder of
it (see [`artifact_store()`](_autosummary/mergeset.storage.html.md#mergeset.storage.artifact_store)), so a new kind never needs a migration.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

```pycon
>>> import os, tempfile
>>> d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
>>> os.environ['MERGESET_DATA_DIR'] = d
>>> app_data_rootdir() == d
True
>>> del os.environ['MERGESET_DATA_DIR']
>>> app_data_rootdir().endswith('mergeset')
True
```

### mergeset.storage.artifact_mall(, rootdir=None, store_factory=None, kinds=('reports', 'evaluations', 'logs', 'fixtures'), app_name='mergeset', binary=False)

All the artifact stores, keyed by kind — a *mall*, in `dol` terms.

Stores are built lazily, so asking for the mall never creates a directory
for a kind you do not use.

* **Return type:**
  [`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)]

```pycon
>>> import tempfile
>>> mall = artifact_mall(rootdir=tempfile.mkdtemp())
>>> mall['evaluations']['a.jsonl'] = '{}\n'
>>> list(mall['evaluations'])
['a.jsonl']
```

### mergeset.storage.artifact_path(kind, key='', , rootdir=None, app_name='mergeset')

Filesystem path for `kind`/`key` under the *local* artifact root.

The escape hatch for the things that genuinely need a path rather than a
store — the append-only evaluation log, and a subprocess told where to write
its own output. Everything else should go through [`artifact_store()`](_autosummary/mergeset.storage.html.md#mergeset.storage.artifact_store),
because a path is exactly the coupling the store exists to remove.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

```pycon
>>> import tempfile
>>> root = tempfile.mkdtemp()
>>> artifact_path('evaluations', 'x.jsonl', rootdir=root) == \
...     __import__('os').path.join(root, 'evaluations', 'x.jsonl')
True
```

### mergeset.storage.artifact_store(kind, , rootdir=None, store_factory=None, app_name='mergeset', binary=False)

A store for one kind of artifact — `str` values, or `bytes`.

* **Parameters:**
  * **kind** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – One of [`ARTIFACT_KINDS`](_autosummary/mergeset.storage.html.md#mergeset.storage.ARTIFACT_KINDS) (any name works; the tuple is the
    set mergeset itself uses).
  * **rootdir** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – Artifact root. Defaults to [`app_data_rootdir()`](_autosummary/mergeset.storage.html.md#mergeset.storage.app_data_rootdir).
  * **store_factory** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)]]) – The backend seam —
    `(kind, rootdir, *, binary) -> MutableMapping`, defaulting to
    `dol` files under `<rootdir>/<kind>/`. Swap it for S3, a
    database, or a dict without touching a single caller.
  * **binary** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – Values are `bytes` rather than `str`. A run’s PDF and its
    Markdown share one directory and differ only in this flag.
* **Return type:**
  [`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)

```pycon
>>> import tempfile
>>> store = artifact_store('logs', rootdir=tempfile.mkdtemp())
>>> store['run-1.log'] = 'all green'
>>> store['run-1.log']
'all green'
```

### mergeset.storage.evaluation_lines(repo, , store=None, rootdir=None, app_name='mergeset')

The append-only lines object backing this repo’s evaluation log.

With no `store`, the local filesystem backend is used directly, because
`open(path, 'a')` is a *true* append and re-writing a growing log on every
evaluation is not. With a `store` (S3, a database, a dict), the log goes
through it like every other artifact — the source of truth is not allowed to
be the one thing that cannot leave the filesystem.

```pycon
>>> import tempfile
>>> lines = evaluation_lines('/x/proj/widget', rootdir=tempfile.mkdtemp())
>>> lines.append({'a': 1}); [d['a'] for d in lines]
[1]
```

```pycon
>>> backing = {}
>>> lines = evaluation_lines('/x/proj/widget', store=backing)
>>> lines.append({'a': 1}); list(backing)[0].endswith('.jsonl')
True
```

### mergeset.storage.evaluation_log_path(repo, , rootdir=None, app_name='mergeset')

Default evaluation-log path for `repo` — in the artifact store.

Deliberately **not** `<repo>/.mergeset/evaluations.jsonl`: that writes a
file capturing one repository’s internals into that same repository, which
is how derived data ends up committed.

`repo` is resolved to an absolute path first, so `'.'` names the current
directory rather than collapsing every project into one `repo.jsonl`.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

```pycon
>>> import tempfile, os
>>> p = evaluation_log_path('/x/proj/widget', rootdir=tempfile.mkdtemp())
>>> os.path.basename(p).startswith('proj-widget-')
True
>>> os.path.basename(p).endswith('.jsonl')
True
```

### mergeset.storage.run_key(repo, , at=None)

A key naming one run of one repository: `<repo-slug>/<timestamp>`.

Reports are keyed by run, not by repository, so a second analysis of the
same repo does not overwrite the first. The 18-PR re-run of an earlier
analysis is exactly the case that made this necessary: the interesting thing
about it is the *diff* against the previous run, and there is no diff if the
previous run was clobbered.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

```pycon
>>> key = run_key('/x/proj/widget', at='2026-09-09T14-00-00Z')
>>> key.endswith('/2026-09-09T14-00-00Z')
True
>>> key.startswith('proj-widget-')
True
```

### mergeset.storage.slash_separated_keys(store, , sep='/')

Make `/` the key separator whatever the platform’s is.

Keys are a store’s public namespace, so they must not change shape with the
operating system: a report written under `'run-a/REPORT.md'` has to read
back under that key on Windows too, and an S3 backend uses `/` regardless.
Without this the same key is two different keys on two machines — the
filesystem leaking through the abstraction the store exists to provide.

A no-op where the separator is already `/`.

* **Return type:**
  [`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)

```pycon
>>> store = slash_separated_keys({}, sep='/')
>>> store['a/b'] = 1; dict(store)
{'a/b': 1}
```

On a backslash platform the *backing* store sees native separators while
callers keep using `/`:

```pycon
>>> backing = {}
>>> store = slash_separated_keys(backing, sep='\\')
>>> store['a/b'] = 1
>>> list(backing)
['a\\b']
>>> list(store), store['a/b']
(['a/b'], 1)
```

### mergeset.storage.slugify(text, , maxlen=48)

A filesystem-safe key naming a run after its repository.

Two path components, not one, so `js/widget` and `py/widget` do
not collide. Two components are still not unique — `/a/b/proj` and
`/c/b/proj` both read as `b-proj` — and two repos sharing one evaluation
log would mix their change ids into one monotone closure, which is a wrong
answer rather than an untidy one. So a short digest of the *full* input is
appended whenever the readable part is not the whole story.

The digest also survives truncation: a long parent directory used to eat the
only component that distinguished anything.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

```pycon
>>> slugify('/Users/me/proj/i/mergeset')
'i-mergeset-ed5b44'
>>> slugify('git@github.com:i2mint/mergeset.git')
'i2mint-mergeset-b35f45'
>>> slugify('.')
'repo-cdb4ee'
```

Different repositories that read alike still get different keys:

```pycon
>>> slugify('/a/b/proj') != slugify('/c/b/proj')
True
```

And a long parent no longer swallows the name:

```pycon
>>> slugify('/x/' + 'a' * 80 + '/repo').startswith('a')
True
>>> 'repo' in slugify('/x/' + 'a' * 80 + '/repo')
True
```


# _autosummary/mergeset.tiers.html.md

# mergeset.tiers

Tiered validation: a cheap oracle screens, an expensive one confirms.

`mergeset` searches a **monotone** predicate — if a set fails, every superset
fails — which is what makes the search tractable at all. This module uses the
second half of that structure, which the package has so far left on the table:

> **The tiers are monotone in each other.** A set that fails a cheap tier
> fails overall, whatever the expensive tier would have said. So a cheap tier
> is a *sound filter*, and an expensive tier only ever needs to run on
> cheap-tier survivors.

That has a consequence worth stating as a lemma, because it is what makes an
unaffordable tier affordable:

> \*\*Every maximal good set of the full oracle is contained in some maximal
> good set of the screen.\*\* (If `S` passes everything then it passes the
> screen, so it sits inside some maximal screen-passing set.)

The maximal screen-passing sets are the **frontier**, and there are usually a
handful of them — four, on a real run of eighteen changes. Everything else the
search touches is *interior*: hitting-set probes and conflict shrinking, dozens
of evaluations, none of which can be the answer. So the question stops being
“which of 2\*\*18 subsets do I dare run browser tests on” and becomes “how few runs
confirm these four”.

The claim is **not** that the expensive tier never touches the interior — that
would be false, and measuring it says so. A conflict visible *only* to the deep
tier has to be shrunk at deep prices, and QuickXplain’s `O(k log(n/k))` queries
for a conflict of size `k` are interior by construction. What holds is the
useful half: a set the screen refutes is never paid for at depth, so the interior
the *screen* explores is free, and deep spending is bounded by the frontier plus
the shrinking that genuine deep-only conflicts force. On eight branches with one
deep-only conflict that is 7 deep runs against 10 screen runs; with no deep-only
conflict it is the frontier and nothing else.

Mechanically that is one composed evaluator with two properties:

- **it short-circuits** — a cheap-tier failure answers the query without paying
  for the deep tier;
- **each tier keeps its own log.** A cheap-tier PASS is not evidence about the
  deep tier, so the two verdicts must not share a cache entry. This is D25 one
  level up: *verified* has to mean **verified at the tier you are claiming**,
  and a set confirmed only to the unit tier says so.

Two stages, and what each costs:

1. **Screen** — the ordinary search ([`mergeset.analyze()`](_autosummary/mergeset.html.md#mergeset.analyze)), with the cheap
   tier as its validator. Pays the whole interior at cheap-tier prices and
   returns the frontier plus every conflict it found.
2. **Confirm** — the same search again, one tier deeper, \*seeded with those
   conflicts\* so it starts almost finished. Its candidates are frontier sets;
   its interior is answered from the screen’s log for free.

If a deep tier is unavailable (no container daemon today) or unaffordable,
stage 2 is skipped rather than degraded, and the answer is labelled with the
depth it actually reached. \*\*A tier that did not run is not a tier that
passed.\*\*

### Functions

| [`analyze_tiered`](_autosummary/mergeset.tiers.html.md#mergeset.tiers.analyze_tiered)(repo, changes, \*, tiers[, ...])   | Screen with the cheap tier, confirm the frontier with the expensive ones.    |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`anytime_answer`](_autosummary/mergeset.tiers.html.md#mergeset.tiers.anytime_answer)(change_ids, conflicts, \*, ...)    | The best validated set so far, plus a sound bound on what is being missed.   |
| [`best_set_including`](_autosummary/mergeset.tiers.html.md#mergeset.tiers.best_set_including)(change_ids, evaluate, \*, ...) | The heaviest validated set that **contains** every change in `must_include`. |
| [`chained_evaluate`](_autosummary/mergeset.tiers.html.md#mergeset.tiers.chained_evaluate)(evaluators)                      | Compose per-tier evaluators into one, short-circuiting on the first failure. |
| [`tier_key`](_autosummary/mergeset.tiers.html.md#mergeset.tiers.tier_key)(tier)                                    | The key-safe form of a tier name.                                            |
| [`tier_lines`](_autosummary/mergeset.tiers.html.md#mergeset.tiers.tier_lines)(repo, tier, \*[, store])               | The append-only lines object backing one tier's evaluation log.              |

### Classes

| [`AnytimeAnswer`](_autosummary/mergeset.tiers.html.md#mergeset.tiers.AnytimeAnswer)(best, best_weight, best_tier, ...)   | The best answer so far, and how much better an answer could still be.   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`Tier`](_autosummary/mergeset.tiers.html.md#mergeset.tiers.Tier)(name, validate[, cost, available])            | One rung of validation, from cheapest to dearest.                       |
| [`TieredAnalysis`](_autosummary/mergeset.tiers.html.md#mergeset.tiers.TieredAnalysis)(tiers, analysis, logs, cost_model)  | Result of a tiered run.                                                 |

### *class* mergeset.tiers.AnytimeAnswer(best, best_weight, best_tier, full_depth, bound, bound_set, gap, optimal, pending=(), spent=<factory>)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

The best answer so far, and how much better an answer could still be.

`bound` is a genuine upper bound, not a hope. Every conflict — found at
any tier, by any pre-oracle — refutes a real set, so the heaviest set that
no known conflict forbids is the heaviest set that *could* still pass. Its
weight is therefore an upper bound on the optimum, and `gap` is what is
still unknown.

`gap <= 0` together with full tier depth is a **certificate**: the
heaviest set nothing refutes has itself been validated, so nothing better
exists. That is a stopping rule rather than a budget running out.

#### best

Heaviest set validated so far, at `best_tier`.

#### best_weight

Its weight (the sum of its changes’ weights).

#### best_tier

Deepest tier that actually ran on `best`; `None` when
nothing has been validated yet.

#### full_depth

True iff every tier ran on `best`. When False, `best` is
a partial claim however good `gap` looks.

### bound, bound_set

The upper bound and the set that realizes it.

#### gap

`bound - best_weight` — what might still be being missed.

#### optimal

`gap <= 0 and full_depth`; nothing better exists.

#### pending

`(set, estimated seconds to confirm)` for candidates not yet
taken to full depth. The answer to “what would closing the gap
cost”.

#### spent

Seconds spent, per tier.

#### summary()

One line a progress display or a report can print.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

```pycon
>>> AnytimeAnswer(frozenset({'a'}), 1.0, 'unit', False, 2.0,
...               frozenset({'a', 'b'}), 1.0, False).summary()
'best 1 change (weight 1.0, confirmed to tier `unit`); bound 2.0; gap 1.0'
>>> AnytimeAnswer(frozenset({'a', 'b'}), 2.0, 'e2e', True, 2.0,
...               frozenset({'a', 'b'}), 0.0, True).summary()
'best 2 changes (weight 2.0, all tiers); provably maximal'
```

### *class* mergeset.tiers.Tier(name, validate, cost=None, available=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

One rung of validation, from cheapest to dearest.

* **Parameters:**
  * **name** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – What this tier is (`unit`, `integration`, `e2e`). It names
    the tier’s own evaluation log and appears in every claim the report
    makes, because “passed the unit tier” and “passed everything” are
    different facts.
  * **validate** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`ValidationOutcome`](_autosummary/mergeset.base.html.md#mergeset.base.ValidationOutcome)]) – `worktree -> ValidationOutcome` — the same contract as every
    validator in [`mergeset.validation`](_autosummary/mergeset.validation.html.md#module-mergeset.validation), so
    [`staged_validation()`](_autosummary/mergeset.validation.html.md#mergeset.validation.staged_validation) and friends drop
    straight in. A tier is *one* validator; the stages *within* it are
    that validator’s own business.
  * **cost** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]) – Declared seconds per run, used until the tier has been timed.
    Worth setting for a tier nobody has run yet: it is what stops a
    cost-ordered scheduler treating an unmeasured tier as cheap.
  * **available** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[], [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)]]) – `() -> bool` — is the infrastructure this tier needs up?
    The honest reason a tier gets skipped is usually not budget but
    absence: no daemon, no display, no credentials. `None` means
    always available, which is the truth for a unit-test tier.

```pycon
>>> from mergeset.validation import merge_only_validation
>>> tier = Tier('merge', merge_only_validation(), cost=0.5)
>>> tier.name, tier.is_available()
('merge', True)
>>> Tier('e2e', merge_only_validation(), available=lambda: False).is_available()
False
```

#### is_available()

Whether this tier can run right now.

* **Return type:**
  [`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)

### *class* mergeset.tiers.TieredAnalysis(tiers, analysis, logs, cost_model, depth_reached=None, skipped=<factory>, spent=<factory>, runs=<factory>, answer=None, must_include=frozenset({}), best_including=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

Result of a tiered run.

`analysis` is an ordinary [`Analysis`](_autosummary/mergeset.analysis.html.md#mergeset.analysis.Analysis) whose
`maximal_sets`, `unverified_sets` and `notes` have been updated to the
depth validation actually reached — so every existing report renders it
unchanged and says the right thing about tiers.

#### best_including *: [frozenset](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#frozenset) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)* *= None*

Heaviest validated set containing every change in `must_include`.
`None` when they cannot all be kept together. A second, differently
constrained answer – never a replacement for the first.

#### cost_lines()

One line per tier: what its log records, and how the tier is priced.

Runs and seconds are read from the tier’s log, so they include earlier
invocations against the same commits, and the line says so. The price
says where it came from – `measured` from the log, `declared` by
the caller, or neither, in which case the model’s default is shown –
because an estimate with no provenance reads as a fact.

* **Return type:**
  [`List`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.List)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

#### depth_reached *: [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)* *= None*

How deep validation actually got, as a tier name.

#### *property* maximal_sets *: [List](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.List)[[frozenset](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#frozenset)]*

maximal sets at the depth reached.

* **Type:**
  The answer

#### must_include *: [frozenset](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#frozenset)* *= frozenset({})*

Changes the caller required in the answer, if any.

#### runs *: [Dict](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]*

Evaluations actually performed, per tier.

#### skipped *: [Dict](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]*

`tier -> why it did not run`. Empty is the normal case.

#### spent *: [Dict](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]*

Seconds spent per tier, measured from that tier’s log.

#### verified_tier(subset)

The deepest tier that recorded an exact PASS for `subset`.

Inference across the monotone closure deliberately does not count. A
passing *superset* is what makes a subset good by inference, and if such
a superset existed it would be the answer instead — so for the purpose
of “was this claim actually run”, only an exact recorded PASS counts.
D25’s rule, applied per tier.

* **Return type:**
  [`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### mergeset.tiers.analyze_tiered(repo, changes, , tiers, cost_model=None, confirm_budget_seconds=None, confirm_max_runs=None, confirm_max_sets=None, must_include=(), on_event=None, \*\*analyze_kwargs)

Screen with the cheap tier, confirm the frontier with the expensive ones.

* **Parameters:**
  * **repo** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – As [`mergeset.analyze()`](_autosummary/mergeset.html.md#mergeset.analyze).
  * **changes** ([`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[`Change`](_autosummary/mergeset.base.html.md#mergeset.base.Change)]) – As [`mergeset.analyze()`](_autosummary/mergeset.html.md#mergeset.analyze).
  * **tiers** ([`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[`Tier`](_autosummary/mergeset.tiers.html.md#mergeset.tiers.Tier)]) – Ordered cheapest-first. The first is the **screen** and pays for
    the whole search interior; each later one confirms what its
    predecessor left standing. One tier reproduces today’s behaviour
    exactly.
  * **cost_model** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`CostModel`](_autosummary/mergeset.cost.html.md#mergeset.cost.CostModel)]) – The price list — a seam. Default:
    [`MeasuredCost`](_autosummary/mergeset.cost.html.md#mergeset.cost.MeasuredCost) seeded from each tier’s
    declared `cost`, then fitted to the durations the tier’s own
    evaluation log records. Measurements from one run price the next.
  * **confirm_budget_seconds** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]) – Wall-clock a deep tier may spend. Admission uses
    the model’s *pessimistic* estimate, because overrunning a budget is
    worse than deferring one evaluation.
  * **confirm_max_runs** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]) – Hard cap on evaluations per deep tier. Takes
    precedence over the budget when both are given.
  * **confirm_max_sets** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]) – Stop a deep tier after this many confirmed maximal
    sets. `1` is “just tell me the single best plan, cheaply”.
  * **must_include** ([`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – Changes that must be in the answer. Answers a *different*
    question alongside the main one — “the best plan that keeps this” —
    and the two can be far apart when the required change conflicts with
    members of the unconstrained best plan. Reported as
    `TieredAnalysis.best_including`; see [`best_set_including()`](_autosummary/mergeset.tiers.html.md#mergeset.tiers.best_set_including).
  * **on_event** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)], [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)]]) – `(event, payload)`. Adds `tier`, `tier_skipped` and
    `anytime` on top of the events [`mergeset.analyze()`](_autosummary/mergeset.html.md#mergeset.analyze) emits, so
    a caller can display the best-so-far after every deep run.
  * **\*\*analyze_kwargs** – Everything else goes to [`mergeset.analyze()`](_autosummary/mergeset.html.md#mergeset.analyze)
    unchanged (`base`, `decompose`, `max_evaluations`, …). Not
    `validate` and not `log`: the tiers own both.
* **Return type:**
  [`TieredAnalysis`](_autosummary/mergeset.tiers.html.md#mergeset.tiers.TieredAnalysis)
* **Returns:**
  A [`TieredAnalysis`](_autosummary/mergeset.tiers.html.md#mergeset.tiers.TieredAnalysis).

### mergeset.tiers.anytime_answer(change_ids, conflicts, , weight, verified, tiers, cost_model=None, remaining_tiers=(), depends_on=None, spent=None, pending_limit=5, bound_search_limit=64)

The best validated set so far, plus a sound bound on what is being missed.

* **Parameters:**
  * **change_ids** ([`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – The universe.
  * **conflicts** ([`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[`frozenset`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#frozenset)]) – Every refuted set, from any tier or pre-oracle.
  * **weight** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]) – `change id -> weight`; a set’s weight is the sum of its own.
  * **verified** ([`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[`Tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Tuple)[[`frozenset`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#frozenset), [`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]]) – `(set, deepest tier that ran on it)` pairs.
  * **tiers** ([`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[`Tier`](_autosummary/mergeset.tiers.html.md#mergeset.tiers.Tier)]) – The tier chain, which is what “full depth” means.
  * **cost_model** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`CostModel`](_autosummary/mergeset.cost.html.md#mergeset.cost.CostModel)]) – Used to price `pending`.
  * **remaining_tiers** ([`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – Used to price `pending`.
  * **depends_on** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]) – `child -> parent` for stacked changes. Without it the
    bound names sets that could never land — a child without its parent
    — so `optimal` never becomes true however much is validated, and
    `pending` prices candidates nobody can run.
  * **bound_search_limit** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – How many minimal hitting sets to consider when
    tightening the bound under stack closure. Closure can only shrink a
    complement, so it breaks the weight ordering the enumeration relies
    on; past this many, the loose-but-sound unclosed bound is used.
  * **spent** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]]) – Seconds per tier, carried through for reporting.
  * **pending_limit** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – How many unconfirmed candidates to price.
* **Return type:**
  [`AnytimeAnswer`](_autosummary/mergeset.tiers.html.md#mergeset.tiers.AnytimeAnswer)

```pycon
>>> tiers = [Tier('unit', lambda w: None), Tier('e2e', lambda w: None)]
>>> answer = anytime_answer(
...     ['a', 'b', 'c'], [frozenset({'a', 'b'})], weight=lambda c: 1.0,
...     verified=[(frozenset({'a', 'c'}), 'e2e')], tiers=tiers)
>>> answer.best_weight, answer.bound, answer.optimal
(2.0, 2.0, True)
```

Same conflicts, but the deep tier never ran. The bound is unchanged and the
answer is explicitly *not* optimal, because a tier that did not run is not a
tier that passed:

```pycon
>>> partial = anytime_answer(
...     ['a', 'b', 'c'], [frozenset({'a', 'b'})], weight=lambda c: 1.0,
...     verified=[(frozenset({'a', 'c'}), 'unit')], tiers=tiers)
>>> partial.optimal, partial.full_depth, partial.best_tier
(False, False, 'unit')
```

### mergeset.tiers.best_set_including(change_ids, evaluate, \*, must_include, conflicts=(), weight=None, depends_on=None, max_evaluations=None, shrink=<function quickxplain>)

The heaviest validated set that **contains** every change in `must_include`.

This is a different question from “the heaviest validated set”, and on real
data the two answers can be far apart. A change that must land — because it
is the one the expensive tier exists for, or because someone has decided it
ships — may conflict with several members of the unconstrained best plan; the
best plan that keeps it is then not a superset of that plan, not a subset,
and not reachable by adding anything to it. It is the complement of a minimal
hitting set that *avoids* the required changes, which is what this
enumerates.

* **Parameters:**
  * **change_ids** ([`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – The universe.
  * **evaluate** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`frozenset`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#frozenset)], [`Evaluation`](_autosummary/mergeset.base.html.md#mergeset.base.Evaluation)]) – The (chained, log-cached) oracle.
  * **must_include** ([`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – Changes the answer must contain. With stacked changes the
    set is closed downward first, since keeping a change means keeping
    what it is built on.
  * **conflicts** ([`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[`frozenset`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#frozenset)]) – Conflicts already known — the point of the exercise is to
    reuse everything the unconstrained search learned.
  * **weight** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]]) – `id -> weight`; candidates are proposed heaviest-first.
  * **depends_on** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]) – `child -> parent` for stacked changes.
  * **max_evaluations** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]) – Budget, in real (uncached) evaluations.
  * **shrink** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`frozenset`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#frozenset)]) – Conflict-minimization strategy.
* **Return type:**
  [`Tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Tuple)[[`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`frozenset`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#frozenset)], [`List`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.List)[[`frozenset`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#frozenset)], [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]
* **Returns:**
  `(best set or None, the conflicts now known, evaluations spent)`.
  `None` means the required changes cannot all be kept: every way of
  resolving the known conflicts drops one of them.

```pycon
>>> from mergeset.base import Evaluation, Verdict
>>> def oracle(subset):                      # 'h' conflicts with 'a' and 'b'
...     bad = {'h', 'a'} <= subset or {'h', 'b'} <= subset
...     return Evaluation(subset, Verdict.FAIL if bad else Verdict.PASS)
>>> best, _, _ = best_set_including('abch', oracle, must_include=['h'])
>>> set_key(best)
('c', 'h')
```

Unconstrained, the answer would have been the three changes that exclude
`h` — bigger, and not an answer to the question that was asked.

### mergeset.tiers.chained_evaluate(evaluators)

Compose per-tier evaluators into one, short-circuiting on the first failure.

This is the lever. A set the cheap tier refutes never reaches the expensive
one, so the search’s interior — every hitting-set probe, every QuickXplain
step — is paid at cheap-tier prices, and the expensive tier is spent only on
sets that survived.

```pycon
>>> def cheap(s):
...     return Evaluation(s, Verdict.FAIL if 'bad' in s else Verdict.PASS)
>>> deep_calls = []
>>> def deep(s):
...     deep_calls.append(set_key(s))
...     return Evaluation(s, Verdict.PASS)
>>> evaluate = chained_evaluate([cheap, deep])
>>> evaluate(frozenset({'bad', 'x'})).verdict.value
'fail'
>>> deep_calls
[]
>>> evaluate(frozenset({'x'})).verdict.value
'pass'
>>> deep_calls
[('x',)]
```

### mergeset.tiers.tier_key(tier)

The key-safe form of a tier name.

The repository half of a log key has always been slugified; the tier half
was interpolated raw, and that is not merely untidy. `e2e` and `E2E` are
two tier names and one file on macOS and Windows — a cheap-tier PASS
answering an expensive-tier question, on the default filesystem of two of
three platforms. `a/b` and `x/../y` reach outside the store entirely.

Case is folded rather than preserved because the collision is the point: two
names differing only in case must be *rejected* as duplicates, never
silently merged into one log. A name that had to be changed at all carries a
short digest of the original, so two different unsafe names cannot be
flattened onto one key either.

`mergeset.storage.slugify` is not reused here: it always appends a digest,
which is right for a long filesystem path and wrong for a name a person
typed and will read back in a report.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

```pycon
>>> tier_key('e2e'), tier_key('E2E')
('e2e', 'e2e')
>>> tier_key('a/b') == tier_key('x/../y')
False
>>> '/' in tier_key('a/b')
False
```

### mergeset.tiers.tier_lines(repo, tier, , store=None)

The append-only lines object backing one tier’s evaluation log.

One log per tier, in the same artifact store as everything else, keyed by
repository *and* tier. Sharing one log between tiers would make a cheap
PASS answer an expensive question, which is the one thing this module
exists to prevent — so both halves of the key are slugified.

```pycon
>>> backing = {}
>>> lines = tier_lines('/x/proj/widget', 'e2e', store=backing)
>>> lines.append({'a': 1}); list(backing)[0].endswith('.e2e.jsonl')
True
```


# _autosummary/mergeset.validation.html.md

# mergeset.validation

Validation functions: does this merged tree actually work?

A validator is any callable `(worktree_path) -> ValidationOutcome`. Four are
shipped — a pytest runner (the default), an arbitrary shell command, a local CI
run via `act`, and “merge-only” — and a user-supplied Python callable is a
first-class fifth option, because the interesting projects always have one more
step than a test command.

Every validator returns a *structured* result, not a bit: which tests failed,
which files they live in, how long it took. The solver uses that to aim its
conflict shrinking at the changes actually implicated, rather than halving
blindly.

A validator may also say *what* it runs: a `validator_fingerprint` attribute,
a short digest of its command, stages, timeout and environment. Every shipped
validator carries one, and the evaluation log stamps it on each row, so a row
recorded by `pytest -x` never answers a question asked of `pytest -m e2e`
(i2mint/mergeset#32). A user callable has none unless it sets one, since only its
author knows what changes its verdicts:
`my_validator.validator_fingerprint = 'smoke-v2'`. Its rows are stamped
`UNKNOWN_FINGERPRINT`, which matches only other such rows. A wrapper made
with `functools.wraps` copies the wrapped validator’s fingerprint along with
its `__dict__`; a wrapper that changes what is checked must set its own.

A fingerprint covers the command’s *text*. When the command runs a script that
lives outside the analysed repository (`python ~/checks/smoke.py`), the
script’s contents are not in it: files inside the repository are pinned by the
commits, files outside it are not. Name such files with `inputs=` and their
contents join the fingerprint, so editing the script retires the verdicts it
gave (i2mint/mergeset#39).

| [`RACY_SECONDS`](_autosummary/mergeset.validation.html.md#mergeset.validation.RACY_SECONDS)          | How old a file's last change must be before its stat may vouch for its contents.                                                                                      |

### Classes

| [`ValidationStage`](_autosummary/mergeset.validation.html.md#mergeset.validation.ValidationStage)(name, command[, ...])   | One step of a staged validation.   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------|

### mergeset.validation.DEFAULT_PYTEST_ARGS *= ('-x', '-q', '--tb=short', '-p', 'no:cacheprovider')*

the answer we need is a bit, and the first failure has it.

* **Type:**
  Fail-fast by default

### mergeset.validation.FILE_DIGESTS *: [Dict](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Dict)[[tuple](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple), [str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]* *= {}*

Content digests of input files, keyed by the file’s path and stat (#42).
Reading an 8.5 GB tree takes about a minute; stat-ing it, seconds. A run
digests its inputs once per validator built and twice around every
evaluation, so all but the first read come from here.

### mergeset.validation.FINGERPRINT_ATTR *= 'validator_fingerprint'*

The attribute a validator carries to say what it runs (i2mint/mergeset#32).

### mergeset.validation.MAX_CACHED_DIGESTS *= 250000*

How many file digests [`FILE_DIGESTS`](_autosummary/mergeset.validation.html.md#mergeset.validation.FILE_DIGESTS) holds before it starts over:
about 110 MiB, room for a large virtual environment.

### mergeset.validation.RACY_SECONDS *= 2.0*

How old a file’s last change must be before its stat may vouch for its
contents. An edit within one timestamp tick of a read leaves size and mtime
as they were (git’s “racy clean” problem); 2 s covers the coarsest common
filesystem timestamps (FAT). Younger files are always read.

### *class* mergeset.validation.ValidationStage(name, command, fingerprint=None, timeout=None, required=True)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

One step of a staged validation.

* **Parameters:**
  * **name** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – What this step is (`setup`, `build`, `test`, `lint`…).
    It ends up in the log and in the report, which is the whole point:
    “failed to build” and “tests failed” are different facts and a
    single pass/fail bit throws away the one you need.
  * **command** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – Shell command, run in the merged worktree.
  * **fingerprint** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]) – Optional `worktree -> str`. When given, the stage is
    skipped if it already ran in this worktree with the same value —
    this is how an expensive dependency install is amortized across
    evaluations instead of being paid every time (keyed on, say, the
    hash of the lockfile).
  * **timeout** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]) – Seconds before the stage is declared failed.
  * **required** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – A failing required stage fails the whole validation and stops
    the sequence (the default). A non-required stage’s failure is
    recorded in `failing_tests` and the set still counts as good —
    for an advisory pass, such as a lint the project runs as a separate
    CI job rather than a gate.

### mergeset.validation.detect_runner(path)

Guess how this project is tested; `None` if nothing is recognizable.

Ordering matters more than it looks. An earlier version checked for a
`tests/` directory in the same breath as `pyproject.toml`, and so
classified a TypeScript repository as pytest and ran pytest in it for a
dozen evaluations before anyone noticed. Manifests decide; a `tests/`
directory is not evidence of a language.

* **Return type:**
  [`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

```pycon
>>> detect_runner('/definitely/not/a/project') is None
True
```

### mergeset.validation.file_fingerprint(\*paths)

A fingerprint function over the contents of the given repo-relative files.

The canonical use is a lockfile: install dependencies again only when
`pnpm-lock.yaml` actually changed between two candidate merges.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### mergeset.validation.fingerprint_of(validate)

What `validate` runs, as a short string – or `None` when it cannot say.

Two validators with the same fingerprint give the same verdict on the same
tree, so an evaluation log may answer one with the other’s rows. `None`
means unknown: such a validator’s rows are recorded as
`UNKNOWN_FINGERPRINT` (see [`recorded_fingerprint()`](_autosummary/mergeset.validation.html.md#mergeset.validation.recorded_fingerprint)), and answer
only other validators that cannot say what they run either.

* **Return type:**
  [`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

```pycon
>>> fingerprint_of(command_validation('make test')) == fingerprint_of(
...     command_validation('make test'))
True
>>> fingerprint_of(command_validation('make test')) == fingerprint_of(
...     command_validation('make check'))
False
>>> fingerprint_of(command_validation('make test')).startswith('command:')
True
>>> fingerprint_of(lambda worktree: True) is None
True
```

### mergeset.validation.flake_tolerant(validate, , retries=1)

Re-run a failing validation `retries` times before believing it.

Monotonicity is a prior, not a law, and flaky tests are the usual way it
breaks. This is the cheap defense; the honest one is
`EvaluationLog.monotonicity_violations`.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`ValidationOutcome`](_autosummary/mergeset.base.html.md#mergeset.base.ValidationOutcome)]

### mergeset.validation.inputs_digest(paths, , cache=FILE_DIGESTS)

A digest of each path’s current contents, keyed by its real path.

These are the files a validator runs that its command text does not
capture: a script outside the analysed repository, a config it reads. A
directory is digested over every file under it (names and contents,
following symlinks, each directory once; `__pycache__`, `*.pyc` and
dot-directories such as `.git` are left out, since running the inputs
writes them), a missing path as `'missing'`
– so creating it later changes the digest too – and one that cannot be
read as `'unreadable'`. Relative paths are resolved against the current
directory, *not* the worktree: files inside the repository are already
pinned by the commits. `paths` is a collection of paths: a lone string is
refused, since it would be read one character at a time.

A file whose path, inode, size, mtime and ctime match an earlier read is
not read again: its digest comes from `cache` (default
[`FILE_DIGESTS`](_autosummary/mergeset.validation.html.md#mergeset.validation.FILE_DIGESTS)), but only once its last change (mtime or ctime,
which no tool can set back) is [`RACY_SECONDS`](_autosummary/mergeset.validation.html.md#mergeset.validation.RACY_SECONDS) older than that read.
`cache=None` reads every file.

Trusting a stat is what `make` and `git` do, with their blind spots: a
second write through a shared `mmap` to an already-dirty page changes
no timestamp, and a network filesystem may serve cached attributes (NFS,
for up to a minute) or stamp times from a clock behind this one. For inputs
edited that way, pass `cache=None`, or set
`mergeset.validation.FILE_DIGESTS = None` to turn the cache off for every
validator (ADR 0035).

* **Return type:**
  [`Dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

```pycon
>>> import tempfile
>>> with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile('w', suffix='.py', delete=False) as f:
...     _ = f.write('print(1)')
>>> before = inputs_digest([f.name])
>>> with open(f.name, 'w') as g:
...     _ = g.write('print(2)')
>>> inputs_digest([f.name]) == before
False
>>> os.remove(f.name)
>>> list(inputs_digest([f.name]).values())
['missing']
```

### mergeset.validation.js_validation(, install='pnpm install --frozen-lockfile', build=None, test='pnpm run test', lint=None, lockfile='pnpm-lock.yaml', timeout=None, inputs=())

A staged validator shaped like a JavaScript project.

Install is fingerprinted on the lockfile so it runs only when dependencies
actually changed; the build, when given, is a required prerequisite of the
tests rather than part of them. `inputs`: files outside the repository
that any step runs (see [`inputs_digest()`](_autosummary/mergeset.validation.html.md#mergeset.validation.inputs_digest)).

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`ValidationOutcome`](_autosummary/mergeset.base.html.md#mergeset.base.ValidationOutcome)]

### mergeset.validation.merge_only_validation()

A validator that accepts anything that merged cleanly.

Useful as a first pass: it costs nothing and still finds every textual
conflict, which on real branch sets is most of them.

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`ValidationOutcome`](_autosummary/mergeset.base.html.md#mergeset.base.ValidationOutcome)]

### mergeset.validation.pytest_validation(, args=('-x', '-q', '--tb=short', '-p', 'no:cacheprovider'), timeout=None, env=None, select_paths=None, inputs=())

A validator that runs the project’s pytest suite, fail-fast by default.

* **Parameters:**
  * **args** ([`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – Passed to pytest. Fail-fast (`-x`) is the default because the
    oracle only needs to know *whether* the set is good.
  * **timeout** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]) – Seconds before the run is declared failed.
  * **env** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)]) – Extra environment variables.
  * **select_paths** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]]) – `worktree -> test paths` — the seam for test-impact
    selection. Return only the tests the merged changes can affect and
    each evaluation gets dramatically cheaper. Default: run everything.
  * **inputs** ([`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Sequence)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – Files outside the repository whose contents change verdicts
    (a shared `conftest.py`, a plugin); see [`inputs_digest()`](_autosummary/mergeset.validation.html.md#mergeset.validation.inputs_digest).

### mergeset.validation.recorded_fingerprint(validate)

The fingerprint a log row records for `validate`: never `None`.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

```pycon
>>> recorded_fingerprint(lambda worktree: True)
```

### mergeset.validation.staged_validation(stages, , env=None, inputs=())

Run an ordered list of [`ValidationStage`](_autosummary/mergeset.validation.html.md#mergeset.validation.ValidationStage) steps, reporting which one failed.

Real projects do not have “the test command”; they have a sequence, and the
steps are not equally interesting. A JS repo may need
`pnpm install` (slow, only when the lockfile moved), then a build (a
*prerequisite* of testing — without it the tests do not even collect, and a
validator that skipped it would report a false failure), then the tests,
then a lint pass.

The failing stage’s name is prefixed onto every reported failure id, so the
log distinguishes `build: ...` from `test: tests/x.ts::y`.

`inputs` names files outside the repository that any stage runs; their
contents join the fingerprint (see [`inputs_digest()`](_autosummary/mergeset.validation.html.md#mergeset.validation.inputs_digest)).

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`ValidationOutcome`](_autosummary/mergeset.base.html.md#mergeset.base.ValidationOutcome)]

# For AI agents

`mergeset` ships artifacts for coding agents alongside its code. This page lists
them, says where each lives in the repository, and points at the
machine-readable copies of this documentation.

## Skills

Skills are folders holding a `SKILL.md` (the [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) format): a description that tells an agent when to use it and a body with the procedure. Install one into your agent with `gh skill` (any host: `--agent claude-code`, `copilot`, `cursor`, `codex`, `gemini`), or use the copy bundled in the wheel.

### `mergeset`

Work out which branches or pull requests can be merged together, and in what order. Use when several changes are in flight on one repository and someone asks which of them can land together, what conflicts with what and why, whether a set of branches can be merged, why two changes cannot go together, or for a landing plan and integration branches. Also use to read or explain an existing mergeset report or evaluation log.

```bash
gh skill install i2mint/mergeset mergeset --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`mergeset/data/skills/mergeset`](https://github.com/i2mint/mergeset/tree/HEAD/mergeset/data/skills/mergeset) (bundled with the pip package).

The bundled skills are also on disk after `pip install mergeset`, under the package’s `data/skills/` directory; link them into an agent without network access with `skill link-skills <that directory>`.

## Subagents

Subagents are Markdown files with a frontmatter (`name`, `description`, `tools`) and a system prompt as the body. Copy one into your project’s `.claude/agents/` (or your agent host’s equivalent) to delegate the task it describes.

### `mergeset-analyst`

Works out which of a repository’s in-flight branches or PRs can be merged together, and explains the result. Use when asked “which of these PRs can land together”, “what conflicts with what”, “can I merge these branches”, “why can’t these two go together”, or when several PRs are open on one repo and a landing order is needed. Also use to explain an existing mergeset report.

Source: [`.claude/agents/mergeset-analyst.md`](https://github.com/i2mint/mergeset/tree/HEAD/.claude/agents/mergeset-analyst.md); tools: `Bash, Read, Grep, Glob`.

## Machine-readable documentation

This site publishes the same documentation in forms that fit an agent’s context window:

- [`llms.txt`](https://i2mint.github.io/mergeset/llms.txt): an index of every page with a one-line description ([llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org) format)
- [`mergeset.md`](https://i2mint.github.io/mergeset/mergeset.md): the whole documentation as one Markdown file
- `<page>.html.md`: a rendered Markdown twin of every page, advertised from each page’s `<head>` with `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">`
- [`objects.inv`](https://i2mint.github.io/mergeset/objects.inv): the Sphinx inventory: a symbol-to-URL index (`sphobjinv convert plain objects.inv -`)
